pins: protocol-survey.md §4/§5 -- packet framing constants and CRC16 (partial: see the gaps object)
rule: Every value below was returned by a function in reference/. Nothing here is hand-computed. Regenerate rather than edit.

constants.note: Values of the reference macros as the compiler sees them. Fixture-plan E4.

opcodes.valid_op_rule: network.c:34 -- valid_op(op) is FIRST_OP <= op <= LAST_OP

packet_layout.note: offsetof() over the TX struct at reference/mochimo-core/src/types.h:606. These are the compiler's numbers, not arithmetic done here.
packet_layout.framing_length_caveat: TXHDRLEN (124) and TXTLRLEN (4) are #defines local to reference/mochimo-core/src/network.c:38-39. They appear in no header, so a port cannot import them; derive the header length from offsetof(TX, buffer) instead, and check it against 124 as this vector does.
packet_layout.on_wire_length_formula: quoted from network.c:301 -- len = TXHDRLEN + get16(tx->len) + TXTLRLEN. Note this is far smaller than sizeof(TX): the buffer is declared WORD16_MAX bytes but only get16(tx->len) of them are transmitted.
packet_layout.crc16_range_formula: quoted from network.c:293 -- put16(tx->crc16, crc16(tx, TXHDRLEN + get16(tx->len))). The CRC covers the fixed header plus the used prefix of buffer, and excludes crc16 and trailer. The receive side checks the identical range at network.c:172 as len - TXTLRLEN.
packet_layout.crc16_placement: quoted from network.c:295 -- memmove(tx->buffer + get16(tx->len), tx->crc16, 4). The 4 CRC+trailer bytes are moved to sit immediately after the used prefix of buffer, NOT at offsetof(TX, crc16). Receive reverses it at network.c:169. A port that lays the packet out by struct offset will produce a packet the network rejects.

vectors.note: the network and trailer fields written by the reference's own put16(). The cheapest possible little-endian regression test: a port that stores these big-endian produces 05 39 / ab cd and every packet it sends is dropped before any signature is examined.
vectors.falsifies: survey §4: multi-byte packet fields are little-endian

vectors.note: put16/get16 round trip over the 16-bit fields used throughout the packet header.
vectors.falsifies: survey §4: get16/put16 are the little-endian 16-bit accessors

vectors.note: the CRC-16/XMODEM published check value: crc16 of the ASCII string "123456789". crc16.h:8 documents this as 0x31c3. If this vector does not read 12739 (0x31c3), the parameters in that comment block -- poly 0x1021, init 0x0000, no reflection, xorout 0x0000 -- do not describe the code, and every other CRC assumption in this port is unfounded.
crc16 of zero bytes. Pins the init value in isolation.
crc16 of a single 0x00 byte. With E2-empty, distinguishes an init-only implementation from one that actually clocks the byte through.
crc16 of 32 zero bytes -- the value most likely to be produced by an uninitialised port.
crc16 of 00 01 02 ... 1f. A non-symmetric input, so a byte-order error in the port cannot cancel out.
crc16 over 64 bytes of buf[i] = i*7+1 (mod 256). Length is the point here: a table-driven port with an off-by-one in its loop bound passes the short vectors and fails this one.

gaps.rule: gen-fixtures calls the reference; it never reimplements it. The entries below have no callable entry point, so they are reported rather than hand-assembled.

E1.wanted: a fully-built OP_TX packet, full bytes
E1.blocker: send_tx(NODE *np, double timeout) at reference/mochimo-core/src/network.c:267 is the only code that frames a packet. It sets version/network/trailer/id/cblock, computes the CRC, memmoves the CRC into place, and then calls send() on np->sd -- all in one function body, with no separable framing helper. Producing the bytes requires a socket, which is neither offline nor deterministic. Several fields it writes (Cblocknum, Cblockhash, Prevhash, Weight) are node globals holding chain state, not protocol constants, so even a captured packet would not be reproducible.
E1.what_is_pinned_instead: packet_layout above gives every field offset and quotes the three framing lines verbatim with file:line, so a port can be written against them and then validated against a live node.

E3.blocker: same as E1 -- framing lives inside send_tx().

E6.wanted: negative verdicts for wrong network, wrong trailer, bad CRC
E6.blocker: the three rejection tests are at network.c:172, :179 and :186, inside recv_tx(NODE *np, double timeout) at network.c:128. recv_tx() calls recv() on np->sd before reaching any of them, so the verdicts cannot be obtained without a socket. The tests themselves are simple enough to quote: get16(tx->crc16) != crc16(tx, len - TXTLRLEN), get16(tx->network) != TXNETWORK, get16(tx->trailer) != TXEOT, each returning VEBAD.

gaps.live_node_roundtrip: out of scope for an offline generator, and the only thing that can actually confirm E1/E3/E6. This is the point at which the port needs a testnet peer.

notes.network_c_174_debug_format_defect: network.c:172 checks crc16(tx, len - TXTLRLEN), which equals TXHDRLEN + get16(tx->len). The pdebug() on the failure path at network.c:174 recomputes it as crc16(tx, TXHDRLEN + len), which double-counts the header and trailer. Only the log line is affected -- the check itself is correct -- but a port that copies the range from the error message rather than from the comparison will be wrong.
notes.align_crc16_field: TX carries a one-byte __align_crc16 field marked UNUSED at types.h:619. It exists to 4-byte-align the crc16/trailer pair inside the struct. It is never transmitted, because the CRC and trailer are memmoved to buffer + get16(tx->len) before sending.
